T + noun: › [ T + noun ] to give something or someone a particular name, especially describing what you think of it, him, or her

T: › [ T ] to change the sounds and speech on a film or television programme, especially to a different language
（尤指用另一種語言）為（影視節目）配音

NONE: › a style of music or poetry connected with reggae in which the main part of the tune is removed and various special effects are added
配上特效的雷鬼音樂；配有雷鬼音樂和音響效果的詩歌

example: She was dubbed by the newspapers "the Angel of Death".
她被報紙稱為「死亡天使」。
I'd rather watch a movie with subtitles than one dubbed into English.
我寧願看帶字幕的原聲電影也不願意看譯成英語的配音電影。
To conceal his identity, the man's voice has been dubbed over (= an actor speaks his words).
為了不暴露他的身分，這個人的聲音都經過了配音處理。

NONE: › a thick soft substance used to make leather soft and waterproof
皮革油（使皮革軟化並防水）

example: It might be better to use dubbin rather than polish on your walking boots.
使用皮革防水油擦你的輕便靴可能比單純擦亮更好。

NONE: C2 thought not to be completely true or not able to be trusted
半信半疑的，可疑的；不確定的；不可信的
C2 feeling doubt or not feeling certain

example: These claims are dubious and not scientifically proven.
這些說法未經科學證實，有些可疑。
He has been associated with some dubious characters.
他曾經與一些可疑人物有交往。
Ruth Ellis has the dubious (= bad) distinction of being the last woman to be hanged in Britain.
露絲‧艾理斯背負著英國最後一個被絞死的女人這樣一個惡名。
I'm dubious about his promises to change his ways.
他承諾將改變行事方式，我對此有些懷疑。

NONE: › mainly UK a type of electronic dance music
迴響貝斯（一種電子音樂）
